title: Snowflake motif — basic
subtitle: A six-pointed snowflake in fine cotton or fingering, 8 cm across
excerpt: Six arms radiate from a tight centre ring, each arm a short sequence of chain and double crochet stitches that taper to a point. The basic snowflake measures 8 cm in 4-ply cotton on a 2.5 mm hook, lies flat without stiffening, and joins in repeating snowflake-grid patterns for window decorations, Christmas tree ornaments, and fine-gauge throws.

content.text: The basic snowflake builds six tapered arms from a 12-dc centre
magic ring

. Each arm is a chain length worked outward to a dc tip, then returned to the ring with a slip stitch. This is the simplest snowflake construction — no picots, no branching — and it produces a clean six-pointed star that reads clearly at small scale. Worked in 4-ply cotton on a 2.5 mm hook, the result is fine and open; in DK on a 4 mm hook it scales to 11 cm for a bolder effect.

Consistency across the six arms is the main challenge: the chain length sets the arm length, so count carefully on each arm. Stiffening with fabric starch is optional for window hangings — 4-ply cotton holds its shape reasonably well without it, though a brief spray helps if the snowflake is to hang for several weeks.

attrs.title: Materials for one snowflake
attrs.body: About 3 g of white 4-ply cotton. A 2.5 mm crochet hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors. Optional: fabric starch.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished basic snowflake measures 8 cm across in 4-ply cotton with a 2.5 mm hook.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), magic ring (MR) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
Pattern
Centre ring
Form a magic ring. Ch 1 (does not count as stitch). Work 12dc into the ring. Sl st to first dc to join. Pull tail to close ring. (12 dc.)
Arms — 6 times

Work 6 arms as follows, attaching each to alternate dc of the ring: *Ch 8. Dc in 2nd ch from hook (arm tip). Ch 3. Sl st back into the ring dc you started from. Sl st into next dc of the ring (skip 1dc, then sl st into the next dc to anchor before starting the next arm).* Repeat from * to * five more times. After 6th arm, sl st to close. Fasten off.

definition.title: Snowflake motif — basic
definition.caption: 12dc magic ring. Six arms: ch-8 out, dc tip, ch-3 back. Arms attached to alternate ring dc.

content.text: Finishing

Weave the starting tail through the centre ring stitches and trim. Weave the finishing tail through the slip-stitch join at the ring. For a hanging ornament, attach a length of thread to one arm tip before weaving in the end.
Care
Handwash in cool water. Pin flat to dry on a foam mat. Re-spray with fabric starch if the snowflake is used as a window hanging.
What to try next

The intricate snowflake (crochet-snowflake-intricate) adds branching picots along each arm for a more elaborate six-pointed form. The joined snowflake (crochet-snowflake-joined) works several basic snowflakes into a motif grid linked at the arm tips.
